headline: Backfired: ISP's spike-shifting cost five times doing nothing
text: ISP tried to cut its transit bill by sending traffic spikes to the pricier Expensive provider, betting its larger free-spike allowance would absorb them. Too many spikes landed there, so Expensive billed at the spike rate: about $2,658, versus $511 for leaving everything on Cheap. The reasoning was sophisticated, but it never projected whether the allowance would last the whole billing cycle.
